label: deepseek-v4-pro
_endpoint_verified: 2026-08-20: 200 on a 32-token probe, served by Azure; max_completion_tokens 384000, quantization unknown
_note: Pinned to azure/us. Endpoint choice was PROBED rather than reasoned about, and the probe overturned the first pick. Reachability on 2026-08-20, one 32-token completion per candidate with provider.only plus allow_fallbacks:false: azure/us, novita/fp8, siliconflow/fp8 and ionstream/fp4 all returned 200; coreweave/fp8 and parasail/fp8, the ONLY two endpoints declaring a 1,048,576 output ceiling, returned a persistent 429 and were the original pin; alibaba/fp8, baidu/fp8 and first-party deepseek returned 404 'no endpoints available matching your guardrail restrictions and data policy'. So the data-residency argument for avoiding first-party DeepSeek is moot: the account's policy already blocks it, along with both China-hosted resellers. azure/us is the reachable endpoint whose hosting matches the posture that policy expresses, which is the same reason vendors.json pins its OpenAI leg to Azure. Its 384,000 ceiling is ample against the 131,072 resolved cap, so the chunking analysis is unchanged. Honest cost of this pin: quantization is 'unknown', so unlike an fp8 pin this leg is not quantization-attributable, and it is the most expensive reachable option at 1.91/3.83 against novita/fp8 at 1.44/2.88. On a run costing about one dollar that premium does not merit trading hosting for it. Documented hand-fallback if Azure rate-limits: novita/fp8, which requires updating this file AND the price row in core/pricing.py together.
_pinning_rationale: Pinning is a CORRECTNESS requirement for this slug, not reproducibility hygiene: OpenRouter serves it with declared output ceilings from 16,384 (DeepInfra) to 1,048,576 (CoreWeave, Parasail), while MODEL_OUTPUT_CAPS records one per-slug value of 393,216. An unpinned route to the low end asks for eight times what the endpoint emits, truncates non-empty, and per this repo's own correction to that table a non-empty truncation is not leg-fatal, so it burns the whole repair budget on every retry. See finding F2 of the run plan.
